analyst_view.overall: Early view: Albacete have turned a dreadful start around under Joseba Etxeberria, who replaced Alberto González in early October, with three straight wins including 3-1 at Leganés, but they are still 21st. Tenerife have drawn four in a row and are dealing with the death of striker Jesús de Miguel after the 2 November match with Andorra. Corpas should be back from his three-match ban by round 16, and Dani Martín's ban should be served against Ceuta on 15 November, so the brief's absence list will likely be out of date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean slightly higher: Albacete have scored seven in their last three under Etxeberria's high-pressing, vertical set-up but still have the second-worst defence (24 conceded), and Tenerife's away games have averaged over three goals. Tenerife's run of 1-1 draws keeps me from going far above the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean a little lower: Álvaro Cervera's Tenerife are happy without the ball (26% possession and no corners against Andorra), and Etxeberria's Albacete attack fast in transition rather than camping in the final third, as at Leganés where they had five corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. I lean higher: Albacete picked up six yellows at Leganés with Etxeberria's aggressive pressing, and Tenerife had three yellows and Dani Martín's red against Andorra. A relegation-threatened home side chasing a fourth straight win adds to the fouling.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.8 shots. I lean lower: Tenerife produce very few shots (five against Andorra) and lean on Enric Gallego, who has scored around half their goals, while Albacete took only 12 at Leganés even in a 3-1 win.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.3 shots on target. I see nothing to move it: Albacete were efficient at Leganés (five on target from 12) and Tenerife put two of five on target against Andorra, which fits a total close to the site's number.
